projectDescription: A TypeScript authorization library that lets you declare a permission catalog in code, enforce it in-process against your own database, and scale from a single application to a federated org — without anything on your request path ever leaving your process.
keyFeatures: Permission catalog declared in TypeScript — every key and scope type verified at build time via template-literal types
In-process checks via can(), canAny(), can.fresh() — nothing on your request path ever calls out
Scope inheritance: grants stored once at a node, ancestor chains walked at check time (O(depth))
Union-only inheritance with personal-only revokes; negative-always-wins precedence
Forward-inclusive wildcards: docs.files.* absorbs future permissions automatically
Static verification (alfiz-verify): typed keys, coverage linting, gate-shape linting, catalog linting
Four mandatory enforcement points: page, navigation, server action, conditional UI
Access requests and approval workflows: auto-approval predicates, named approvers, management-layer routing
Headless administration components: permission tree, role editor, grant/revoke pickers, approvals queue
Snapshot API: one provider round-trip for synchronous in-map() checks
Prisma storage driver with structural delegate interface (no hard @prisma/client dep)
Alfiz Cloud: hosted Diwan dashboard, admin seats, federation, provisioned connectors
publicApiSurface: alfiz-verify.config.json: catalog, include, exclude, gateNames, visibilityNames, serverFilePatterns, forbidClientIdentifiers
